title: Switching to tenor when Andrew Brown was ill
summary: The sick Brown's solos pass to Thomas on tenor; when Brown returns he's given alto.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: So one night, Brown was ill. And we...
He was an alto saxophone player.

Yeah, a saxophone player. He was one of the original guys, see. And he was ill. So here we're sitting up on the stand, the third alto and the first alto. So I suggested to the guys, I said... I suggested to Cab, "Let me play the tenor saxophone. It's better, if you've only got two saxophones, for it to be alto and tenor." So I picked up the saxophone and started playing, reading... And all the solos that Brown was playing, I could play them, because I just had an ear. In my days of playing, I could play a chord to whatever I heard. And I had been hearing the arrangements all the time; they wasn't new to me. And I played all the solos. So the band started thinking that I played the solo a little better than Brown. So when... Brown was out maybe for close to a week. So when Brown
came back, the way they made the switch, they told Brown that he sounded better on alto than I did. So that's how we made the switch.
